thread:
ana: Heads-up, hit an OOM during nightly kvcache prefetch run on 8G A100s with the small-chat workload. looks like fragmentation + large split allocations.
raj: ugh, which knobs were we using? expandable_segments was off? max_split_size_mb?
maria: last known config from canary: expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=128, garbage_collection_threshold=0.5
ana: output snippet:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 536870912 bytes (requested 512MiB)
Active allocations: 6.2 GiB, reserved: 7.5 GiB
Allocator state: free fragments: 14, largest_free=24MiB, avg_free=8MiB
KV-cache growth: +40MiB/s
```
kevin: that largest_free=24MiB suggests large split allocations cause fragmentation; max_split 128MB lets large allocations fragment the arena.
sophie: agree. for this workload we get many mid-sized tensors (~40-80MB) and the current max_split forces single big splits.
raj: proposed quick experiment matrix:
- toggle expandable_segments=true (let segments grow instead of splitting)
- test max_split_size_mb in [32, 64, 96]
- gc threshold in [0.25, 0.4] (trigger earlier GC to free small fragments)
maria: will run this tonight as 3x permutations, will tag bench runs with labels: prefetch-bandit/expseg-<bool>/max<xx>/gc<yy>
ana: add a probe-mode where prefetch does a tiny probe allocation to detect free contiguous space before committing a prefetch chunk. call it prefetch_probe_rate=0.05 (5% of prefetches).
kevin: I can attach a small perf tracer to capture kernel-selection/alloc waterfall and kv cache hit rates. need traces for: baseline, expseg=true, max_split=32.
perf-bot: CI bench queued: prefetch-bandit/expseg-true/max32/gc025 (job id: 90512)
maria: quick command I'm using:
```
./ci/bench/prefetch_bandit.sh --workload small-chat --runs 4 \
  --max-split 32 --expandable-segments true --gc-threshold 0.25 \
  --probe-rate 0.05 --tag expseg-true-max32-gc025
```
ana: if expandable_segments helps, that means we prefer contiguous growth over splits -> kernel routing should also be aware (smaller contiguous allocs change preferred kernels).
raj: keep an eye on KV cache warmup time and hit-rate: earlier fragmentation caused kv warmup to fail and we saw 15% lower hits.
kevin: tracing note: when fragmentation spikes we also saw more memcpy/kernels falling back to slower attendance path at long seq lengths. I'll capture a 30s window at peak.
sophie: timeline: maria runs tonight, kevin pulls traces tomorrow morning, we reconvene at 11:00 to decide changes for canary.
maria: started first job (expseg=true,max=32,gc=0.25) now, ETA ~45m. I'll post raw logs + allocation map when done.
ana: thanks. if that looks good we can flip canary knob and watch ops metrics for regressions. :eyes:
kevin: FYI I added a small patch to the allocator to log "split_ratio" metric when splitting occurs, should help quantify how often large splits happen vs contiguous growth.
ana: perfect. also add an alert: prefetch_hit_rate drop > 10% within 15m after knob flip.
maria: job finished, uploading artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/prefetch-bandit/expseg-true-max32-gc025/90512
maria: quick summary: OOM disappeared, fragmentation reduced, avg largest_free=90MiB, split_ratio down 78%, kv hit-rate up +6%
kevin: attaching sample flame for the run (kv warmup window): s3://redwood-profiles/90512/flame.svg
ana: nice. let's run one more with max_split=64 and expseg=false to compare.
maria: queued that now.
perf-bot: CI bench queued: prefetch-bandit/expseg-false/max64/gc025 (job id: 90513)
raj: if expseg=true is winning we should consider defaulting to true for small-GPU SKUs (<=16GB) and add a safety switch for large-model paths.
sophie: noted. i'll draft a short playbook for the rollout and rollback signal thresholds (oom rate, kv hit-rate, latency p95).
ana: thanks team. reconvene when we have the second run. :thumbsup:
